bottom_line: In RE-LY, dabigatran 150 mg twice daily vs warfarin reduced stroke or systemic embolism (relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82).
implications: Based on the reported relative risk 0.66 (95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82) and event rates 1.11% per year vs 1.69% per year, the document supports that dabigatran 150 mg twice daily was associated with a lower rate of stroke or systemic embolism than warfarin in this trial; it does not support a reduction in major bleeding versus warfarin for dabigatran 150 mg (3.11% per year vs 3.36% per year; P = 0.31).

major_points.text: Randomized noninferiority trial comparing two fixed doses of dabigatran (blinded) vs adjusted-dose warfarin (open-label) in atrial fibrillation patients at risk for stroke.
major_points.quote: In this noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned 18,113 patients who had atrial fi- brillation and a risk of stroke to receive, in a blinded fashion, fixed doses of dab- igatran — 110 mg or 150 mg twice daily — or, in an unblinded fashion, adjusted-dose warfarin.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was stroke or systemic embolism.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was stroke or systemic embolism.

major_points.text: Median follow-up was 2.0 years with 99.9% complete follow-up and 20 patients lost to follow-up.
major_points.quote: The median duration of the follow-up period was 2.0 years, and complete follow-up was achieved in 99.9% of pa- tients, with 20 patients lost to follow-up.

major_points.text: Major bleeding was lower with dabigatran 110 mg vs warfarin, but not significantly different with dabigatran 150 mg vs warfarin.
major_points.quote: The rate of major bleeding was 3.36% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 2.71% per year in the group receiving 110 mg of dabigatran (P = 0.003) and 3.11% per year in the group receiving 150 mg of dabigatran (P = 0.31).

major_points.text: Hemorrhagic stroke rates were lower with either dabigatran dose than with warfarin.
major_points.quote: The rate of hemorrhagic stroke was 0.38% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 0.12% per year with 110 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001) and 0.10% per year with 150 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001).

absolute_effects.text: Intracranial bleeding: 0.74%/yr (warfarin) vs 0.30%/yr (dabigatran 150 mg) vs 0.23%/yr (dabigatran 110 mg).

subgroups.text: No significant interaction was seen with treatment effect of dabigatran in the subgroups shown in Figure 2.
subgroups.quote: For the subgroups shown in Figure 2, no signifi- cant interaction was seen with the treatment ef- fect of dabigatran (at either dose).

subgroups.text: No significant interaction between treatment effect and presence or absence of long-term therapy with a vitamin K antagonist.
subgroups.quote: There was no significant interaction between the treatment ef- fect of dabigatran and presence or absence of long- term therapy with a vitamin K antagonist.

harms.text: Major gastrointestinal bleeding rate was higher with dabigatran 150 mg than with warfarin.
harms.quote: There was a significantly higher rate of major gastrointestinal bleeding with dabigatran at the 150-mg dose than with warfarin.

harms.text: Dyspepsia occurred more often with dabigatran than with warfarin.
harms.quote: Dyspepsia occurred in 348 patients (5.8%) in the warfarin group and in 707 patients (11.8%) and 688 patients (11.3%) in the 110-mg and 150-mg dabigatran groups, respective- ly (P<0.001 for both comparisons)

harms.text: Discontinuation at 2 years was 21% in each dabigatran group vs 17% with warfarin.
Hepatobiliary serious adverse events were 0.5% (dabigatran 110 mg), 0.6% (dabigatran 150 mg), and 0.5% (warfarin).

criticisms.text: Major bleeding rate with warfarin was higher than in some previous trials, partly due to a more inclusive definition of major bleeding in this study.
criticisms.quote: The rate of major bleeding with warfarin was higher in our study than in some previous trials.11,13,14 This is partly explained by the more inclusive defi- nition of major bleeding in our study.

criticisms.text: Dose tailoring concept was not specifically tested in the trial.
criticisms.quote: These findings suggest that the dose of dabigatran could potentially be tailored to take into consideration the risk characteristics of a spe- cific patient, although this concept was not spe- cifically tested in our trial.
